## Proof

Let $DO!$ denote the model completion of the theory $DO$. We use two standard facts:

**Fact 1 (Model completeness).** A model completion is model complete. Hence every embedding between two models of $DO!$ is elementary.

**Fact 2 (Types are realized).** Every complete $n$-type $p$ of $DO!$ (i.e. every maximal set of formulas in $n$ free variables consistent with $DO!$) is realized in *some* model of $DO!$. This follows from the Completeness Theorem: the expanded theory $DO! \cup \{\varphi(\bar x) : \varphi \in p\}$ is finitely satisfiable (hence consistent), so it has a model $\mathfrak M \models DO!$ in which some tuple $\bar a$ realizes $p$.

---

Now let $\mathfrak A$ be the countable model of $DO!$ into which every model of $DO!$ embeds. Fix $n$ and let $p$ be any complete $n$-type of $DO!$.

By Fact 2, there exist a model $\mathfrak M \models DO!$ and a tuple $\bar a \in M^n$ realizing $p$ in $\mathfrak M$. By the hypothesis on $\mathfrak A$, there is an embedding
$$f : \mathfrak M \hookrightarrow \mathfrak A.$$
By Fact 1 (model completeness of $DO!$), this embedding is **elementary**. Therefore for every formula $\varphi(\bar x)$,
$$\mathfrak M \models \varphi(\bar a) \iff \mathfrak A \models \varphi(f(\bar a)).$$
Since $\bar a$ realizes $p$ in $\mathfrak M$, the tuple $f(\bar a) \in A^n$ realizes $p$ in $\mathfrak A$.

Thus **every** complete $n$-type of $DO!$ is realized in $\mathfrak A$.

Since $\mathfrak A$ is countable, $A^n$ is countable. Each $n$-tuple in $A^n$ realizes exactly one complete $n$-type, so the number of $n$-types realized in $\mathfrak A$ is at most $|A^n| = \aleph_0$. Because every $n$-type of $DO!$ is realized in $\mathfrak A$, the total number of $n$-types of $DO!$ is at most $\aleph_0$.

Therefore $DO!$ has only countably many $n$-types for every $n$. $\blacksquare$
